entry.name: mc.rect~
entry.description: Use the rect~ object to generate an anti-aliased rectangle wave.

arguments.name: frequency
arguments.description: First argument sets the initial frequency of the oscillator. The default is 0.

arguments.name: pulse-width
arguments.description: An optional second argument sets the pulse width. The default is 0.5.

messages.name: float
messages.description: In left inlet: Sets the frequency of the oscillator.In middle inlet: Sets the pulse width of the oscillator. Signal is wrapped into the range 0-1. A value of 0.5 will produce a rectangular wave that spends equal amounts of time on the positive and negative edges of its cycle.

messages.name: int
messages.description: In left inlet: Sets the frequency of the oscillator.In middle inlet: Sets the pulse width of the oscillator. Signal is wrapped into the range 0-1. A value of 0.5 will produce a rectangular wave that spends equal amounts of time on the positive and negative edges of its cycle.

messages.name: signal
messages.description: In left inlet: Sets the frequency of the oscillator.In middle inlet: Sets the pulse width of the oscillator. Signal is wrapped into the range 0-1. A value of 0.5 will produce a rectangular wave that spends equal amounts of time on the positive and negative edges of its cycle.In right inlet: (optional) A sync signal. When the control signal crosses from below 0.5 to above 0.5, the oscillator resets itself. Aobject works well for this purpose. The classic use is to set this control signal to your fundamental frequency and "sweep" the left frequency input in a range somewhere several octaves higher than the fundamental.

messages.name: synctrig
messages.description: The wordfollowed by a floating-point number changes the value at which the object resets itself (i.e., when the input signal crosses from below the specified number to being above it,will reset itself).
